about.title: Bellflower Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Bellflower packs a lot of traffic into a small footprint. Roughly 78,000 residents share the same surface streets, and public collision records for 2025 count 357 injury crashes in the city, 513 people hurt, and 10 lives lost. Clark Avenue, Bellflower Boulevard, Woodruff Avenue, and Alondra Boulevard appear most often in those reports, and Friday evenings between 5 and 7 tend to see the heaviest concentration. If one of those numbers now describes your week, the practical steps matter more than the statistics. Get checked by a doctor even if you feel shaky rather than injured. Photograph the vehicles, the intersection, and any skid marks before the scene is cleared. Keep every bill and note every missed shift. And when the other driver's insurer calls asking for a recorded statement, you are allowed to decline until you have spoken with a lawyer. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Bellflower drivers, passengers, and pedestrians with an independent California personal injury attorney who works on contingency, and the introduction is free.

items.title: Deadlines Explained Early
items.desc: California gives most car accident victims two years to file, but a claim involving a city bus, public works truck, or other government vehicle can require notice in as little as six months. The attorney you're matched with sorts that out before time becomes a problem.

items.title: Partial Blame Doesn't End the Case
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can recover even if you were partly responsible; your share of fault simply reduces the amount. An independent attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your percentage.

items.title: Nothing Owed Unless You Recover
items.desc: Attorneys in our network handle car accident cases on contingency, so there are no upfront fees. California also places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost enjoyment of life in ordinary car crash claims.

items.question: I was hit near Woodruff Avenue and Alondra Boulevard. Does the intersection matter to my claim?
items.answer: The location itself doesn't decide fault, but it shapes the evidence. Busy Bellflower corridors often have nearby businesses with cameras and multiple witnesses, and that footage can be overwritten within days. Acting quickly to preserve it is one of the first things an attorney will want to do.

items.question: The other driver's insurance adjuster wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it is usually wise to wait until you've talked with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to shift blame or minimize injuries. Politely decline, take down their contact information, and let a lawyer handle the conversation.

items.question: What if I think I was partly at fault for the crash?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, so being partially responsible does not bar you from recovering. If you're found 30 percent at fault, for example, your compensation is reduced by 30 percent rather than eliminated. Don't assume you have no case before an attorney reviews the facts.
